title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic attempt at a 'tame' analysis situs. There is a set M of 'multiplicités' (strata, manifold-like pieces) and a set F of 'figures' (stratified objects). Three relations are in play:
- X ≤ F: X is a (multi)stratum or sub-figure of F. Page 80 introduces F̃ (written F̄ on that page) for {X ∈ M : X ≤ F}.
- F ≪ G: G is a refinement or subdivision of F.
- ≼: a weaker 'contained in / covered by' relation. In the earlier ad hoc reading, ≼ was simply inclusion of figures.
The axioms C1–C8 constrain these relations.

Goal. Pages 80–82 aim at a corollary of the new axiom C8: if F ≪ G and G ≪ F, then F = G. In other words, refinement is antisymmetric, so ≪ is an order relation. The key lemma is: if F ≪ G ≪ F (or more generally X ≪ G ≤ F with X a stratum of F), then every stratum X of F is a stratum of G, i.e. X ≤ G_X.

Set-up on this page (top diagram). Start from X ≪ G ≤ F with X ≤ F. Take the 'inverse images' (pullbacks) of the sub-figure X of F:
- G_X: the sub-figure of G lying over X.
- F_X and Ḡ_X: the corresponding pieces in F and in Ḡ (Ḡ is the closure-type figure; H = Ḡ, H' = G_X in a crossed-out passage).
These are characterised by a universal property, cited from 'la prop. p. 70'. A crossed-out first attempt tried to get X ≪ G_X directly from that universal property.

The chain written on the page is
  G_X ≤ X,
  Ḡ_X ≤ F_X,
  with X sitting under them.
The stated aim is: 'On a à montrer : X ≤ G_X'.

Axiom C8 (stated here, made precise on p. 82). Let X ∈ M and Φ, Ψ ∈ F.
- (a) If X ≤ Φ ≼ X, then X = Φ.
- (b) If X ≼ Ψ ≤ X, then X = Ψ.
Informally: a multiplicity cannot be a stratum of a strictly larger figure contained in it, nor contain a figure strictly finer than itself that is a sub-figure of it. It is a 'no proper self-subdivision' or rigidity axiom for manifold strata.

Proof sketched at the bottom.
1. Apply (a) to X ≤ F_X ≼ X to get X = F_X. This step is spelled out on p. 82.
2. Then X ≤ Ḡ_X ≤ F_X = X forces X = Ḡ_X.
3. Hence X = Ḡ_X ≼ G_X ≤ X, and (b) gives X = G_X.
4. So X ≤ G.

By symmetry this yields F̃ ⊂ G̃ and G̃ ⊂ F̃, hence F ≤ G ≤ F and F = G. Page 82 remarks that C8 is necessary (and probably sufficient) for ≪ to be an order relation.

What it serves. This is the order-theoretic foundation (antisymmetry of refinement) for an axiomatic theory of stratified 'figures', in the spirit of the tame-topology programme of Esquisse §5.
errors: Step 2 tacitly uses antisymmetry of ≤ (from X ≤ Ḡ_X ≤ F_X = X it concludes X = Ḡ_X). This is presumably an earlier axiom, but it is not cited.
The relation between Ḡ_X and G_X used in step 3 (Ḡ_X ≼ G_X) is not justified on this page. It presumably comes from the universal property of p. 70.
Applying C8(a) requires X ≤ F_X and F_X ≼ X. The second is asserted without proof here (it is given on p. 82).
The page is a draft: several false starts are crossed out, and the notation shifts between Ḡ, G̃ and the inverse images.

ideas.what: Axiomatic system of 'figures' (stratified objects) and 'multiplicités' (strata) with three relations: stratum-of (≤), refinement (≪) and containment (≼)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / poset of stratifications under refinement; cf. o-minimal structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s–90s); tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984)
ideas.where_published: Only the programme appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this axiomatics is unpublished.

ideas.what: Axiom C8: a multiplicity admits no proper self-subdivision or self-containment, i.e. X ≤ Φ ≼ X implies X = Φ, and dually
ideas.modern_name: rigidity / minimality of strata, needed for antisymmetry of the refinement preorder
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather)

ideas.what: Pullback (inverse image) of a stratum X of F along a refinement G of F, with a universal property
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a stratification to a stratum / induced stratification

ideas.what: Lemma: if X ≪ G ≤ F and X is a stratum of F, then X is a stratum of G; hence refinement is antisymmetric
ideas.modern_name: antisymmetry of the refinement order on stratifications

missed.claim: The page is part of an unpublished axiomatic order-theoretic framework for tame topology (figures, multiplicités, relations ≤, ≪, ≼, axioms C1–C8). This would be the first concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' foundations announced in Esquisse §5. The mathematics on this particular page is a routine antisymmetry argument.
missed.quote: C8 a) ... X ≤ Φ i.e. X est subdivision de X ... on a X = Φ ; X ≼ Ψ, X multiplicité, Ψ figure, donc X = Ψ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing this poset-style axiomatics with o-minimal structures and with recent stratified/exit-path ∞-categorical approaches could show whether Grothendieck's axioms capture a different notion of tameness. That would be of historical and possibly foundational interest, but this page alone contains nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine order-theoretic bookkeeping (antisymmetry of refinement via a rigidity axiom) inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft. The framework itself is of historical interest, but this page has no notable new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit G_X la deux figure de G image inverse de ... deux figure X de F' should likely read 'la sous-figure de G image inverse de la sous-figure X de F' (whole passage crossed out).
'X est fig. de F' more likely reads 'X est str[ate] de F'.
'On a vu ici: pourquoi X ≤ G_X' more likely reads 'On a à montrer : prouvons X ≤ G_X'.
'X ad[?] [?]' under the chain probably reads 'X est multiplicité'.
'Comme[?]' at the left of the crossed line is plausibly 'Cas où ...'.
The relation in the last line is ≼ (curly), i.e. 'X ≼ G_X ≤ X'. The line above reads 'X ≤ (≤) Ḡ_X ≤ F_X = X', with an overwritten ≤.
In the C8(a) line, 'X ≤ Φ' is followed by a parenthetical; 'si Φ' likely abbreviates 'et Φ ≼ X'.
